parsed.explanation: The combined regime is driven by national measures that bind every traveller. Entry screening refuses cases with any document or sex-evidence discrepancy, and a fraud finding can carry lifetime ineligibility. Passport sex-marker restrictions are in force, and documented immigration custody includes forced labour, beatings and severe sexual abuse of transgender men. National threat framing, minor-care subpoenas and federal facility policy add exposure. The state layer is less restrictive: no statewide adult restroom or care ban, no sodomy law, and marriage recognition. It is offset by the absence of state or municipal anti-discrimination or hate-crime recourse for visitors outside four municipalities, and by no sourced violence data. The national exposure, with documented custody harm, outweighs the state's comparatively open adult regime.

entry_documents.exposure: Cable instructs refusal of cases with document discrepancy or doubt about sex; suspected wilful misrepresentation can support permanent lifetime ineligibility. Passport marker restrictions in force; passports reported confiscated or blocked.
entry_documents.protection: Refusal is not automatic; fraud finding requires four elements with limited waivers. Civil-liberties suit pending; some orders enjoined.
entry_documents.interaction: Refusal or detention at entry can lead into immigration custody, and national rules govern entry regardless of the state's permissive adult regime.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented immigration custody abuse: forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement, severe sexual abuse of transgender men. Federal corrections adopted conversion-therapy-style policies from 2026; transgender prisoner counts no longer reported.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Courts have partly enjoined some orders; no documented operative remedy producing change in custody.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry refusal or fraud allegation flows into immigration custody; federal custody placement policy applies regardless of state law.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National executive order restricts access to government-funded single-sex facilities by identity. State has no statewide adult restroom or changing-room ban; one school district's policy applies to students only.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State-level adult facility access is not barred; trespass-arrest statute exists in other states, not this one.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal facility rules bind national buildings and pass through entry and custody; the state layer is silent on adult facilities.

care_services.exposure: Draft state medical rule would classify under-18 transition care as unprofessional conduct (not operative); national subpoenas of hospital records for under-19 patients; proposed federal insurance exclusion for under-18s.
care_services.protection: No statewide ban on adult gender-affirming care; the draft is not in effect and awaits review and comment.
care_services.interaction: Adult care is open at state level; national data-sharing and funding rules can still reach any patient records.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups for priority neutralisation; cash-reward guidance uses 'radical gender ideology' language; executive orders direct investigation of schools and teachers.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Strategy states powers will not target people who merely disagree; no documented targeting of visitors.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat framing is national; it raises perceived risk for advocates and visitors connected with them more than for ordinary travellers.

minors_guardians.exposure: Minor in transition faces restricted youth care (27 states ban; draft state rule; proposed federal rule), hospital record subpoenas, and school-policy exposure in one district. Guardians face no documented criminal exposure in this state.
minors_guardians.protection: State restrictions on minors' care are not yet operative; state adult care remains open; no state minor-travel custody rule documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: A minor's documents and care needs can meet national entry screening; a guardian with mismatched documents faces the same entry exposure as an adult.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state-level hate-crime enhancement for gender identity; no state or municipal recourse outside four municipalities; trespass arrest in another state documented; 37 states lacked gender-identity anti-bias statutes as of 2019.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Four municipalities prohibit gender-identity discrimination in employment, housing and public accommodation; national hate-crimes statute covers gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Recourse is local-only; a visitor outside those four municipalities has no discrimination remedy in hotels or restaurants.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No sourced enforcement of municipal ordinances; no trans-specific violence count or homicide baseline; no sourced bias-crime guidance from police; national litigation unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Marriage recognised; sodomy law repealed; no adult care ban; document changes available for residents; civil-liberties litigation active.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unknowns are not treated as safety; violence axis is undocumented and not assessed.

anchor_checks.comparison: Both involve universal entry-based exclusion with few effective remedies. The 0.35 anchor's exclusion is routine and ends without custody, whereas this dossier documents immigration-custody sexual abuse and a lifetime-ineligibility pathway, so this case sits lower on custody harm. The state's open adult regime keeps it above the anchor overall.

Similar: biometric or document-based discretionary checks with narrow anti-discrimination recourse and detention for verification. This dossier adds documented custody abuse and fraud-ground refusals, while the 0.45-A case has no documented custody abuse. It sits slightly lower, with the state's facility and marriage openness keeping it near that level.

Secondary screening, discretionary refusal and administrative-only penalties appear in both. The 0.55 anchor has no documented custody abuse and a clearer appeal route. This dossier is lower on custody and enforcement and has less functioning remedy, so it sits below 0.55.

parsed.synthesis: A visitor's exposure is set mainly by national entry and custody rules, not by the state's adult-permissive layer. A document discrepancy can trigger refusal, a fraud finding with possible lifetime ineligibility, and then immigration custody, where abuse is documented. Passport restrictions and federal facility rules apply across the country. The state contributes no adult bathroom or care ban, no sodomy law and marriage recognition. Those are offset by the absence of state or municipal recourse outside four cities and by the lack of sourced violence data, which is treated as undocumented. Pending litigation and draft youth-care rules are not operative. Overall, the combined regime is elevated risk, clearly below the open-regime anchors.
